newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - loses 1/4 to 3/8 on day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - loses 1/4 to 3/8 on day.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices shed about 1/4 to 3/8 point Monday in extremely quiet action, traders said.
Market participants said activity was light, with a few bids on bid-wanted lists providing about the only activity for the session.
One trader said the week's new issue calendar might help liven things up later in the week.
"I think the calendar could actually help us," the trader said. "I think the market could get some footing, especially from the big North Carolina issue."
North Carolina plans to sell the largest issue of the week, a $450 million competitive sale on Wednesday.

The full competitive calendar totals $746 million for the week, while negotiated offerings total $2.1 billion in 33 sales. The largest is a $300 million Jefferson County, Ala., issue through Raymond James & Associates Inc.
Monday's lower market reflected declines in the Treasury market, though traders said a late day improvement in government bonds did not help munis.
The government long bond fell 11/32 at 97-12/32 to yield 6.83 percent.

Traders said there was little reaction to one of the day's main economic indicator, the National Association of Purchasing Management. The report showed manufacturing rose to 53.1 in February from 52.0 in January. A reading below 50 signals that the economy is contracting.
In futures, the June municipal contract lost 7/32 to finish at 114, while June T-bond futures dropped 9/32 to 110-5/32. The MOB spread widened to 123 ticks from 121 at the close on Friday.
Actively traded issues in the secondary market included North Carolina Eastern Mountain Power Agency MBIA 5-3/8s of 2024, which lost 3/8 as bids moved to 98.
Houston, Texas, water and sewer system FGIC 5-1/4s of 2025 were bid at 5.74 percent net, up two basis points.
